text: On the grey flats off the Skerrow coast, the new Bank wind farm has begun to turn in earnest, its 72 turbines now standing in a wide crescent beyond the fishing lanes. The array, built by Calder Vale Renewables after six years of surveys and hearings, stretches across a seabed once known more for wreck markers than for industry. Local harbormaster Elin Marr said the first full-power run had been “oddly quiet, like the horizon had learned a new trade.” The project, first approved in 2019 and completed this autumn, is expected to supply enough electricity for 380,000 homes, a figure that would have seemed fantastical when the bay was still mapped chiefly by gulls and tides.
